interactive_hooks.description_from_source_comment: Keeps Tab / Shift+Tab inside the given containers while `active`, closes on Escape, and restores focus to the previously focused element afterwards. Several containers are allowed because the overlay menu shares focus with the header (which holds the close button).
True while the element intersects the viewport (expanded by `rootMargin`).
Subscribes to a CSS media query. Returns `false` during server rendering and hydration (getServerSnapshot), then the real value — no hydration mismatch.

Scroll reveal. Usage:
…
One IntersectionObserver is shared by the whole page. When an element is 8% visible it receives `.is-visible` (animations.css) and is no longer observed. The `.reveal` class is in the server HTML, but it only hides content once `.motion-ready` is on , so crawlers and no-JS visitors always see everything.

WAI-ARIA tabs keyboard model (automatic activation): arrow keys move and select, Home/End jump to the ends, only the selected tab is in the tab order. Used by the product suite, solutions and delivery-pathway tabs.

One shared, rAF-batched scroll/resize loop for every scroll-driven effect. Each subscriber is called once per frame with the viewport size. It should only READ layout (getBoundingClientRect) and return a function that WRITES (style.setProperty, classList). All reads run before all writes, so the page never forces a synchronous layout between effects — the same "one read phase, one write phase" rule the design's script used. Effects write CSS custom properties directly on DOM nodes: scrolling never triggers a React re-render.
